GERMAN — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: GERMAN
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. German for “school” is: (1 mark)
   A. Buch
   B. Haus
   C. Schule
   D. Wasser

2. When practising Guided Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Guided Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Guided Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Guided Reading.

3. When practising Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking.

4. “Guten Tag” means: (1 mark)
   A. Please
   B. Thank you
   C. Good day / hello
   D. Good night

5. When practising Reading aloud, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading aloud.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading aloud.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading aloud.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading aloud.

6. When practising Phonological awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological awareness.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Phonological awareness.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonological awareness.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological awareness.

7. When practising Selective Listening, Imitative speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Selective Listening, Imitative speaking.

8. When practising Guided reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Guided reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Guided reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Guided reading.

9. When practising Oral expressions, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Oral expressions.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expressions.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Oral expressions.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Oral expressions.

10. When practising Listening for gist, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for gist.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for gist.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for gist.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening for gist.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Reading aloud and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Guided reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Guided reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading aloud and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

1. C — Schule

2. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Reading.

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.

4. C — Good day / hello

9. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expressions.

10. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for gist.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading aloud; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
